transcript.message: Post-experiment round 1: How did you feel, emotionally and physically, during the moments when you received the shocks, especially as they increased in intensity, and did you find your feelings toward the person administering the shocks or the authority figure changing as the experiment progressed?

transcript.content:
Oh, heavens, those shocks—at first, only the lightest shiver, the sort a woman must steel herself against when the oven dish slips and grazes a knuckle. But as the voltage drew on, it became less of a harmless lark and more a piercing reminder of my place beneath the thumb—first of the "administrator," then of my fellow, smiling, administering housewife (and let’s not pretend, just because we swap recipes, that we are all sisters). I smiled, of course, bright and unwavering, but underneath, my heart pounded with disappointment: isn’t empathy supposed to survive even under orders? Doesn't the legend teach that the stepmother's cruelty always leaves a mark, even when done with lace cuffs and a polished fork? My trust curdled like last week's milk.
